parts.title: My first roller coaster
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I have always been afraid of fast rides. When my friends went on roller coasters, I waited at the bottom and held their bags. At fourteen, I felt that it was time to change.

Last summer, my cousin Alex invited me to a big theme park. "Come on," he said. "You will love the Mega Loop." The queue was one hour long, and with every step, my heart beat faster. People were screaming, and the train looked like a huge snake.

When we sat down, a worker checked our safety bars and smiled. I closed my eyes, and my hands felt cold. Then the train began to climb, very slowly, up and up. At the top, there was a short silence, and then we shot down at a terrifying speed. I screamed all the way round, but I could not stop laughing.

When the ride was over, I could hardly stand. "Again!" I shouted. We rode the Mega Loop four more times, and by the end, I was shouting with joy. Alex says that I am now braver than he is. I am not sure that is true, but I am going back next year.

questions.explanation: She waited at the bottom and held their bags.

options: Frightened as the ride came nearer

parts.title: The story of the funfair
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Funfairs have been popular for hundreds of years. [1] In the Middle Ages, people travelled to markets, and the traders often brought musicians and acrobats to attract crowds.

Over time, the entertainment became more important than the trading. [2] By the nineteenth century, fairs had swings, merry-go-rounds and small steam engines to pull the rides.

Then, in the twentieth century, the first big amusement parks opened. [3] Families could now spend a whole day in one place, with food, rides and shows all together.

Today, the biggest theme parks have roller coasters that reach speeds of over a hundred and fifty kilometres an hour. [4] Designers use computers to test every turn, and the rides must pass many safety checks.

Despite all this technology, the old funfair is still alive. [5] Every summer, small fairs with simple games and sweets arrive in towns and villages.
sentences: At first, they were only a part of the market days.
Most of these were built near large cities or at the seaside.
Those fairs sometimes stay for just a week before they move on.
People paid a few coins to play games or to win a prize.
Safety is the most important thing for the people who build them.
It was always very difficult to find an empty space.

gaps.explanation: At first, funfairs were part of the market days, which leads to the example from the Middle Ages.
People paid coins to play games and win prizes, which shows the entertainment becoming more important.
The big amusement parks were built near large cities, and families could then spend a whole day there.
Safety is the most important thing, and the next sentence says designers test every turn.
Those fairs stay for a week and then move on, which links to the small fairs in towns every summer.

parts.title: Tips for a day at a theme park
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: A day at a theme park can be great fun, but it can also be tiring. Here are some tips to help you [1] the most of it. First, arrive early. The park is less crowded in the morning, [2] you can go on more rides without waiting. Second, wear comfortable shoes, because you will walk many kilometres. Third, bring a bottle of water and some snacks, [3] food in the park is often expensive. If you are with young children, make a plan [4] you start, and decide which rides are suitable for their age. Remember to put on sun cream, even when the weather is cloudy. And finally, do not try to do everything. It is better to enjoy a few rides [5] to rush around all day. A relaxed visitor is [6] happy visitor.

gaps.explanation: Make the most of it means use it as well as you can.
The park is less crowded, so you can go on more rides: result.
Bring water because food is expensive: reason.
Make a plan before you start: time order.
Better to enjoy a few rides than to rush: comparison.
A relaxed visitor is a happy visitor: indefinite article.

parts.title: A talk about a famous theme park
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: philippa
turns.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Today, I would like to tell you about the biggest theme park in my country. It opened thirty years ago, and every year, about five million people come to visit. The park covers an area as big as two hundred football fields. There are more than fifty rides, and the oldest one is a small wooden carousel. The tallest roller coaster is a hundred metres high, and it goes at ninety kilometres an hour. The park employs about three thousand people, and in the summer, many students work there as ride attendants. There are also twenty restaurants and a big firework show every night at ten. If you decide to visit, I recommend buying your tickets online, because it is cheaper. And please, wear comfortable shoes, because you will walk a lot. Most visitors say that the best moment of the day is the fireworks at the end.

parts.title: An interview with a ride operator
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Ikenna, you work at a theme park in the summer. What do you do exactly?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: I operate the Space Wheel. I help people get into their seats, check the safety bars and press the start button. Then I watch the ride for the whole time.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the best part of the job?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: The smiles. When people come off the ride laughing, I feel really happy. It makes the long, hot days worth it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: And the worst?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: The heat. In July, the temperature goes up to thirty-five degrees, and we have to wear a thick uniform. I drink about four litres of water every shift.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever get nervous people?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: All the time. Last week, a boy was crying in the queue. I told him that he did not have to go, but he said that he wanted to try. He loved it in the end.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you ever had any problems on the ride?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: Once, the ride stopped because of a storm. We had to wait for twenty minutes, and we gave everybody free drinks.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Would you recommend this job to students?

turns.speaker: o
turns.text: Yes. You meet many new friends, and the money is good. Just be ready to stand for eight hours a day!
